summary: The Torah has thirty-six sins that are so serious that one who does them on purpose gets kares. This mishnah lists all of them.

chunks.en: There are thirty-six sins in the Torah that bring kares.
chunks.explain: Kares is a very serious punishment from Hashem.
chunks.st: There are thirty-six cases in the Torah with regard to which one who performs a prohibited action intentionally is liable to receive excision from the World-to-Come [karet].

words.note: Sins whose punishment is kares, being cut off.

chunks.en: One who sins with his mother,
chunks.st: They are: One who engages in sexual intercourse with his mother;

chunks.en: or with his father's wife,
chunks.st: or with the wife of his father,
chunks.stMore: even if she is not his mother;

chunks.en: or with his daughter-in-law.
chunks.st: or with his daughter-in-law.

chunks.en: One who sins with another man,
chunks.st: The same punishment is imposed on a man who engages in intercourse with another male [hazekhur],

chunks.en: or sins with an animal,
chunks.st: or who copulates with an animal;

chunks.en: and a woman who sins with an animal.
chunks.st: and a woman who brings an animal upon her

chunks.en: One who sins with a woman and her daughter,
chunks.st: The same punishment is imposed on one who engages in intercourse with a woman and her daughter,

chunks.en: or with a married woman.
chunks.st: or with a married woman.

chunks.en: One who sins with his sister,
chunks.st: The same punishment is imposed on one who engages in intercourse with his sister,

chunks.en: or with his father's sister,
chunks.st: or with his father’s sister,

chunks.en: or with his mother's sister,
chunks.st: or with his mother’s sister,

chunks.en: or with his wife's sister,
chunks.st: or with his wife’s sister,

chunks.en: or with his brother's wife,
chunks.st: or with his brother’s wife,

chunks.en: or with the wife of his father's brother,
chunks.st: or with the wife of his father’s brother, or with the wife of his mother’s brother,

chunks.en: or with a niddah.
chunks.st: or with a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: One who curses Hashem's Name, and one who serves idols,
chunks.st: And these too are liable to receive karet: One who blasphemes the name of Heaven, and one who worships an idol,

chunks.en: and one who gives some of his children to the Molech idol,
chunks.st: and one who gives of his children to Molekh (see Leviticus 20:1–5),

words.note: An idol that people served by passing children through fire.

chunks.en: and a ba'al ov,
chunks.st: and a necromancer,

words.note: A ba'al ov claims to talk with the dead.

chunks.en: one who breaks Shabbos,
chunks.st: and one who desecrates Shabbat.

chunks.en: and one who is tamei and ate holy food,
chunks.st: And the same is the punishment of one who is ritually impure who ate sacrificial food;

chunks.en: and one who goes into the Beis HaMikdash while tamei,
chunks.st: and one who enters the Temple while ritually impure;

chunks.en: one who eats chelev,
chunks.st: and one who eats forbidden fat,

words.note: Certain fat of an animal that the Torah forbids to eat.

chunks.en: or blood, or nosar,
chunks.st: or consumes blood, or eats meat left over from an offering after the time allotted for its consumption [notar],

words.note: Meat of a korban left over after the time to eat it.

chunks.en: or piggul, and one who shechts and offers a korban outside the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: or eats meat of an offering that was sacrificed with the intent to consume it after its designated time [piggul]; and one who slaughters offerings and offers them up outside the Temple.

words.note: A korban made unfit by planning to eat it after its time.

chunks.en: one who eats chametz on Pesach,
chunks.st: And these too are liable to receive karet: One who eats leavened bread on Passover,

chunks.en: and one who eats or does work on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: and one who eats or performs prohibited labor on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: one who mixes the special oil,
chunks.st: And the same is the punishment of one who blends the anointing oil
chunks.stMore: according to the specifications of the oil prepared by Moses in the wilderness (see Exodus 30:22–33);

chunks.en: and one who mixes the ketores,
chunks.st: and one who blends the incense
chunks.stMore: according to the specifications of the incense used in the Temple service for purposes other than use in the Temple;

words.note: The special incense burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and one who rubs himself with the shemen hamishchah.
chunks.st: and one who applies the anointing oil to his skin.

words.note: The special oil Moshe made to anoint the Kohanim and the Mishkan.

chunks.en: Also Korban Pesach and bris milah, which are mitzvos to do.
chunks.st: And one is liable to receive karet for failure to fulfill the mitzva of bringing the Paschal offering and the mitzva of circumcision, which unlike the cases of prohibitions enumerated in the mishna, are positive mitzvot.

summary: For these sins, one who does them on purpose gets kares, and one who does them by mistake brings a chatas. Rabbi Meir and the Sages say which sins are different.

chunks.he: עַל אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִים עַל זְדוֹנָם כָּרֵת,
chunks.en: For these sins, one who does them on purpose gets kares,
chunks.st: For any of these prohibitions, one is liable to receive karet for its intentional violation

chunks.en: and one who does them by mistake brings a chatas,
chunks.st: and to bring a sin offering for its unwitting violation.

chunks.he: וְעַל לֹא הוֹדַע שֶׁלָּהֶן אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
chunks.en: and one who is not sure if he sinned brings an asham taluy,
chunks.st: And for their violation in a case where it is unknown to him whether or not he transgressed, he is liable to bring a provisional guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: which provides provisional atonement until he discovers whether or not he transgressed.

words.note: Hanging: brought when one is not sure he sinned.

chunks.en: except for one who makes the Beis HaMikdash or its holy things tamei,
chunks.st: This is the halakha for all of the transgressions listed above except for one who defiles the Temple, i.e., he enters the Temple while ritually impure, or partakes of its consecrated items

chunks.en: because he brings a korban oleh v'yored.
chunks.st: In these cases he does not bring a provisional guilt offering because he is obligated to bring a sliding-scale offering for a definite transgression.

words.note: A korban that goes up and down: a rich person brings more, a poor person less.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: also one who curses Hashem does not bring them,
chunks.st: The halakha is the same even with regard to the one who blasphemes,

chunks.en: as it says (Bamidbar 15),
chunks.st: as it is stated
chunks.stMore: with regard to the sin offering:

chunks.he: תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה,
chunks.en: "You shall have one law for one who does it by mistake."
chunks.st: “You shall have one law for him who performs the action unwittingly” (Numbers 15:29),

chunks.en: This leaves out one who curses Hashem,
chunks.st: excluding one who blasphemes,

chunks.en: because he does not do an action.
chunks.st: as he does not perform an action but sins with speech.

summary: When a woman loses a pregnancy, sometimes she brings a korban that is eaten, sometimes a korban that is not eaten, and sometimes no korban at all. This mishnah lists the first group.

chunks.en: Some women bring a korban and it is eaten,
chunks.st: There are some women who bring a sin offering of a woman after childbirth and the offering is eaten by the priests.

chunks.en: and some bring one but it is not eaten,
chunks.st: And there are some women who bring a sin offering but it is not eaten.

chunks.en: and some do not bring one at all.
chunks.st: And there are some women who do not bring a sin offering at all.

chunks.en: These bring a korban and it is eaten:
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: The following women bring a sin offering and it is eaten by the priests:

chunks.en: A woman who lost a pregnancy that looked like an animal, a wild animal, or a bird.
chunks.st: One who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to a domesticated animal, one who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to an undomesticated animal, or one who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to a bird;

words.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: it must have the shape of a person.
chunks.st: She does not bring a sin offering unless the fetus has the form of a person.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a pregnancy shaped like a sandal,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who miscarries a sandal fetus,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one that has the form of a flat fish;

words.note: A flat shape, like a flat fish.

chunks.en: or the afterbirth,
chunks.st: or if she miscarries the placenta;

chunks.en: or a sac with a shape inside,
chunks.st: or an amniotic sac in which tissue developed;

chunks.en: or one that came out in pieces,
chunks.st: or a fetus that emerged cut, i.e., in pieces;

chunks.en: and also a maidservant who lost a pregnancy,
chunks.st: and likewise a Canaanite maidservant, owned by a Jew, who miscarried;

chunks.en: brings a korban and it is eaten.
chunks.st: in all these cases she brings a sin offering and it is eaten by the priests.

summary: Sometimes a woman brings a korban but it is not eaten, because we are not sure she really needed it. Rabbi Yosei says when two women may bring one korban together.

chunks.en: These bring a korban, but it is not eaten:
chunks.st: And these women bring sin offerings but their sin offerings are not eaten:

chunks.en: A woman who lost a pregnancy and does not know what it was,
chunks.st: One who miscarries and does not know the nature of what she miscarried;

words.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy

chunks.en: and also two women who lost pregnancies,
chunks.st: and two women who miscarried,

chunks.he: אַחַת מִמִּין פְּטוּר וְאַחַת מִמִּין חוֹבָה.
chunks.en: one of a kind that needs no korban, and one of a kind that needs a korban.
chunks.st: in a case where one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is exempt from bringing an offering and the other one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is liable to bring an offering, and they do not know which miscarried which type.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָלְכוּ זוֹ לְמִזְרָח וְזוֹ לְמַעֲרָב.
chunks.en: When is this? When one went to the east and the other to the west.
chunks.st: When is their sin offering not eaten? It is when both women went to different places within the Temple to bring their offerings, e.g., this woman went to the east and that woman went to the west.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן עוֹמְדוֹת כְּאַחַת,
chunks.en: But if both of them were standing together,
chunks.st: But if both of them were standing together,

chunks.en: they bring a korban, and it is eaten.
chunks.st: both of them together bring one sin offering, and it is eaten.

summary: Some women who lose a pregnancy do not bring a korban at all, because what came out was not a baby. Rabbi Shimon argues about one case.

chunks.en: These do not bring a korban:
chunks.st: These women do not bring a sin offering:

chunks.en: A woman who lost a sac full of water,
chunks.st: A woman who miscarries an amniotic sac full of water,

chunks.en: full of blood,
chunks.st: or one full of blood,

chunks.en: or full of colored things,
chunks.st: or one full of different colors;

chunks.he: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים,
chunks.en: a woman who lost something like fish, grasshoppers, or creeping creatures,
chunks.st: and likewise a woman who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to fish, or grasshoppers, or repugnant creatures, or creeping animals;

chunks.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy on the fortieth day,
chunks.st: and a woman who miscarries on the fortieth day of her pregnancy;

chunks.en: and a baby born through the side.
chunks.st: and a woman who gives birth by caesarean section.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says she must bring a korban for a baby born through the side.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems a woman liable to bring a sin offering in the case where she gives birth by caesarean section.

summary: After a girl is born, the mother brings her korban on the eighty-first day. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about a woman who loses a pregnancy on the night before that day: does she need another korban?
stIntro: A woman who gives birth to a daughter counts fourteen days during which she is ritually impure. That is followed by sixty-six days during which she remains ritually pure even if she experiences a flow of blood. The Torah obligates a woman to bring her offering on the eighty-first day (see Leviticus 12:1–6). If the woman miscarries another fetus before that day, she is not required to bring an additional offering.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a pregnancy on the night before the eighty-first day,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who miscarries a fetus on the night of, i.e., preceding, the eighty-first day,

words.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say she does not need another korban,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem her exempt from bringing a second offering

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say she does.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem her liable to bring a second offering.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to Beis Shammai,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "What is the difference between the night of the eighty-first
chunks.st: What is different between the night of the eighty-first

chunks.en: and the eighty-first day?
chunks.st: and the day of the eighty-first?

chunks.en: If they are the same for tumah,
chunks.st: If they are equal with regard to the halakhot of ritual impurity,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the blood flow of this woman on the eighty-first night renders her ritually impure and all the standard strictures of ritual impurity apply to her,

chunks.en: shouldn't they be the same for the korban?"
chunks.st: will the two time periods not be equal with regard to liability to bring an additional offering as well?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד,
chunks.en: "No! If you said this about a woman who lost a pregnancy on the eighty-first day,
chunks.st: No, there is a difference between that night and the following day. If you said with regard to a woman who miscarries on the eighty-first day
chunks.stMore: that she is obligated to bring an additional offering, this is logical,

chunks.en: that is because she came into a time that is
chunks.st: as she emerged into a period that is fit

chunks.en: fit to bring a korban.
chunks.st: for her to bring her offering.

chunks.en: Will you say the same about one who lost on the night before the eighty-first,
chunks.st: Would you say the same with regard to a woman who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first day,

chunks.en: who did not come into a time that is
chunks.st: where she did not emerge into a period that is fit

chunks.en: fit to bring a korban?"
chunks.st: for her to bring her offering,
chunks.stMore: as offerings are not sacrificed at night?

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "But look at a woman who lost a pregnancy on the eighty-first day
chunks.st: But let the case of a woman who miscarries on the eighty-first day

chunks.en: that falls on Shabbos. It proves our point:
chunks.st: that occurs on Shabbat prove that this distinction is incorrect,

chunks.en: she did not come into a time that is fit
chunks.st: as she did not emerge into a period that is fit

chunks.en: to bring a korban, and still she must bring a korban!"
chunks.st: for her to bring her offering because individual offerings are not sacrificed on Shabbat, and nevertheless she is obligated to bring an additional offering.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים
chunks.en: "No! If you said this about a woman who lost a pregnancy on the eighty-first day
chunks.st: No, there is a difference between these cases. If you said this ruling with regard to a woman who miscarries on the eighty-first day

chunks.en: that falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: that occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: that is because, even though Shabbos is not
chunks.st: the reason is that although Shabbat is unfit for

chunks.en: fit for the korban of one person,
chunks.st: the sacrifice of an individual offering,

chunks.en: it is fit for a korban of the whole community.
chunks.st: it is fit for the sacrifice of a communal offering
chunks.stMore: whose time is fixed, e.g., the daily offering.

chunks.en: Will you say the same about one who lost on the night before the eighty-first,
chunks.st: Would you say the same with regard to a woman who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first day,

chunks.en: when the night is not fit, not for a korban
chunks.st: as the night is completely unfit,

chunks.en: of one person and not for a korban of the community?
chunks.st: since neither an individual offering nor a communal offering is sacrificed at night?

chunks.en: And the tumah of the blood does not prove anything,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai add: And as for the ritual impurity status of the blood, i.e., Beit Hillel’s opinion that the two time periods are equal with regard to the halakhot of ritual impurity, this does not prove
chunks.stMore: what the halakha should be with regard to offerings,

chunks.en: because a woman who lost a pregnancy before her eighty days were complete
chunks.st: as with regard to a woman who miscarries before the completion of the term of eighty days,

chunks.en: is tamei,
chunks.st: her blood is impure
chunks.stMore: like the blood of a woman after childbirth,

chunks.en: and still she does not need to bring a korban."
chunks.st: and nevertheless she is exempt from bringing the offering.

summary: A woman who needs many korbanos of birds may bring just one and then eat from korbanos. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught this to bring down the price of birds.

chunks.en: A woman who is not sure about five
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who has in her case uncertainty concerning

chunks.en: times of being a zavah and not sure about five births,
chunks.st: five births, and likewise a woman with regard to whom there is uncertainty concerning five irregular discharges of blood from the uterus [ziva],

words.note: Times of being a zavah, a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: brings one korban,
chunks.st: she brings one offering,

chunks.en: and then she may eat from korbanos,
chunks.st: and then she may partake of the meat of offerings.

chunks.en: and she does not have to bring the rest.
chunks.st: And the remaining offerings are not an obligation for her.

chunks.en: If she had five births for sure,
chunks.st: If she experienced five definite discharges of a zava or

chunks.en: or five times of being a zavah for sure,
chunks.st: five definite births,

chunks.en: she brings one korban,
chunks.st: she brings one offering,

chunks.en: and then she may eat from korbanos,
chunks.st: and then she may partake of the meat of offerings.

chunks.en: but she still has to bring the rest.
chunks.st: And the remaining offerings are an obligation for her.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָמְדוּ קִנִּים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּדִינְרֵי זָהָב.
chunks.en: Once, a pair of birds cost a gold dinar in Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: There was an incident where the price of nests, i.e., pairs of birds, stood in Jerusalem at one gold dinar,
chunks.stMore: as the great demand for birds for the offerings of a woman after childbirth and a zava led to an increase in the price.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: "I swear by this house of Hashem,
chunks.st: I swear by this abode of the Divine Presence

words.note: The Beis HaMikdash, where the Shechinah rests.

chunks.en: I will not go to sleep tonight
chunks.st: that I will not lie down tonight

chunks.en: until they cost silver dinars!"
chunks.st: until the price of nests will be in silver dinars.

chunks.en: He went into the Beis Din and taught:
chunks.st: Ultimately, he entered the court and taught:

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חָמֵשׁ לֵדוֹת וַדָּאוֹת,
chunks.en: A woman who has five births for sure,
chunks.st: A woman who has in her case five definite discharges of a zava or

chunks.en: or five times of being a zavah for sure,
chunks.st: five definite births

chunks.en: brings one korban,
chunks.st: brings one offering,

chunks.en: and then she may eat from korbanos,
chunks.st: and then she may partake of the meat of offerings.

chunks.en: and she does not have to bring the rest.
chunks.st: And the remaining offerings are not an obligation for her.

chunks.en: That same day, the price of a pair of birds went down to a quarter of a silver dinar.
chunks.st: And as a result, the price of the nests stood that day at one-quarter of a silver dinar, as the demand for nests decreased.
